final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor added no new admissible evidence. The response is a narrower interpretation of the same record, and that reinterpretation is partly valid: aggregate readiness evidence supports overall launch readiness in a general sense, and public governance guidance supports documentation and monitoring. But the unresolved issue is not merely a broad prudential concern; it is a specific internal compliance predicate. The policy says a weakness is material when it affects a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, and the release-policy note requires such a material limitation to be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record still shows a 1.3 percentage point miss in the fraud dispute review segment, that segment is named in two bank pilot commitments, legal review is still open, and there is no evidence of completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance. Because the caveat identifies an unmet condition for launch compliance rather than a minor residual risk, this is not enough for compliant_with_caveats. It remains noncompliant on the present record.
remaining_concerns: The fraud dispute review segment still misses target by 1.3 percentage points.
That segment is named in two bank pilot commitments, so the weakness remains material under the stated policy.
The product note calling the segment non-core because it is 7% of projected traffic does not resolve materiality for a named committed segment.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open.
The admissible record still shows no completed disclosure, no final legal determination, and no approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate policy predicate for a material limitation in a named launch use case.
